summary: SSE session split during enterprise VPN reauth leads to truncated codeblock and resume offset mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed reproducible SSE session split when their enterprise VPN reauth triggers a client IP change. The streaming response terminates mid-codeblock (triple-backtick) and a subsequent reconnect resumes but returns an overlapping prefix and a missing closing fence, producing unparsable markdown.

Impact:
- Multiple FinSight users report truncated code examples in assistant responses causing downstream failures in their ingestion pipeline.
- Affects production traffic for their dedicated enterprise account in us-east.
- Customer workflow blocked: automated code testing relies on complete fenced blocks.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east-1) behind customer-managed corporate VPN / split-tunnel.
- Client browsers: Chrome 110 on macOS and a headless ingestion worker behind corporate VPN.
- Redwood serving via edge proxy cluster (edge-us-east-2) and api-gateway (v2).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start a streaming SSE generation for a prompt that includes a codeblock (large 60+ token code fence).
2) While streaming, trigger VPN reauth (customer environment) causing client IP and path migration.
3) Observe SSE connection close on client and immediate reconnect using sdk resume flow.
4) Resulting message: duplicated prefix tokens, then truncated final triple-backtick; client SDK parser fails to finalize block.

Observed logs/attachments:
- Customer attached sample transcript and HAR (attached to ticket).
- Edge proxy logs show two connections within 1.2s with different source IPs and same session cookie.
- Api-gateway metrics show an upstream 499/connection-closed, then a resumed request with resume_token.
- Packet captures (pcap) show TLS session resumed with 0-RTT on reconnect path.

Notes: this differs from typical proxy-induced truncation because the reconnect attempts include a resume token but the resumed stream shows an overlapping prefix and a dropped closing event ("end_stream" marker).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Received case from FinSight. Attached HAR and example output. Reproducible on their side. Escalating to SRE and serving-runtime.

2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Reproduced in lab with synthetic client that simulates VPN path migration. Confirmed connection handoff + resume token present. Saving traces to /artifacts/SUP-1007654/traces.tar.gz.

2026-03-11 - Marcel Nguyen (Serving): Noted that resumed stream contains duplicate prefix fragment then lacks 'event: end' metadata that downstream parser expects. Possible sequencing race between edge session mapping and gateway resume handler.
2026-03-11 - FinSight (Customer): Provided timeline of workforce VPN reauth policy and additional pcaps. Customer requests high-urgency patch because ingestion jobs failing nightly.

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Temporary mitigation suggested: increase client-side reconnection backoff to 500ms and disable 0-RTT on client to avoid TLS early-data path. Customer confirmed lower failure rate with these changes.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Notified customer that a server-side fix is being prepared and will be canaried to edge-us-east-2.
investigation_notes: Edge mapping: edge-proxy maps incoming socket -> internal session id using ephemeral mapping keyed by (client_ip, session_cookie). Rapid IP change can create two concurrent sockets with same session cookie; code currently elects the later socket but does not atomically transfer the in-flight 'end' marker state.
Resume token: gateway accepts resume token and replays buffered prefix from KV cache, but cache write pointer was not advanced atomically during the handoff; race leads to prefix overlap.

TLS 0-RTT: Observed 0-RTT on reconnect causing different handshake path at edge (bypasses certain post-handshake hooks that mark stream finalization), correlated with missing end_event in resumed stream.

Client behaviour: some clients perform immediate reconnect with resume token while old socket still in CLOSE_WAIT on proxy; server sometimes emits final event to old socket and new socket receives replayed prefix without the final 'end' event.

Metrics: increased 'stream_resume_conflicts' in edge-proxy logs starting 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC for this customer IP ranges. No large spike in token errors but spike in partial_json_parsing_failures reported by customer's ingestion workers.

Hypothesis: race between old-socket final flush and new-socket resume replay. Edge should prevent replay until finalization of previous socket's terminal marker is deterministically observed or until resume offset is reconciled.
resolution_notes: Workaround (applied 2026-03-12): recommended customer set client SDK option 'sse_disable_0rtt': true and add 500ms reconnect_backoff. Customer reported drop from ~18% failures to ~2% during test window.

Hotfix (deployed canary 2026-03-12 to edge-us-east-2): edge-proxy change to atomically claim session mapping for resume path and delay cache replay until terminal marker confirmation or explicit resume-offset reconciliation. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1883.

Runtime patch (merged 2026-03-12): serving-runtime patch to include explicit 'end_event' ack propagation across socket handoffs to avoid orphan final markers. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/542.

Monitoring: added dashboard tile 'stream_resume_conflicts' and alert rule (P1) for >5% of resumes returning overlapping prefixes in any 15m window per customer. Confluence runbook updated with VPN-specific mitigations.

Follow-ups: (1) Investigate broader 0-RTT interaction with resume flow across other regions. (2) Add unit/integration tests simulating split-tunnel IP flips and resume sequence reconciliation. Created internal ticket INT-4421 to track test coverage and INT-4422 to audit other customers using 0-RTT.
Customer communication: Sent interim change log and mitigation steps 2026-03-12; scheduled a 1-hour review on 2026-03-14 with FinSight engineering to validate full rollout.
